description.narrative:
Regional Asia Pacific Programme: Advancing Just Transitions to Climate Resilient and Nature-Positive Societies (RAPP2) is a regional program in Southeast Asia and South Asia run by RWI together with partners in the region. The intervention will last from May 2024 until December 2026.
RAPP2 is a continuation of Sida's previous support for RWI's Regional Asia Pacific Program (2017-2024). Sweden's support for RAPP2 is also a phase-out support for RWI's regional program in Asia and the Pacific.
RAPP2 builds on previous results from the regional program and strengthens capacity in South and Southeast Asia to achieve equitable and sustainable development. The overall objective of RAPP2 is to enhance enabling environments for just transitions to climate-resilient and nature-positive societies that are grounded in human rights and gender equality in the Asia-Pacific region. More specifically, RAPP2 will:
1) Strengthen the enabling environment for integrating and addressing human mobility risks, grounded in rights- and gender-based approach, in Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation (CCMA) Initiatives.
2) Strengthen the enabling environment for improved access to environmental justice in Southeast Asia.
3) Strengthen the enabling environment for increased business compliance with EU regulation on human rights and environmental due diligence in the biofuels and critical minerals sectors.
These objectives will be achieved by:
- strengthening universities' capacity to deliver evidence- and rights-based education in law, trade and extraction of minerals and biofuels, climate migration, and disaster risk reduction to the next generation of national and regional entrepreneurs, experts and leaders;
- strengthening the capacity of regional organizations and National Human Rights Institutes (NHRIs) to identify deficiencies and uphold environmental and human rights.
The Revision of the Philippines’ Procedural Rules on Environmental Cases is a smaller component of RAPP2 which is being conducted jointly with the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) and the Asia Research Institute on Environmental Law (ARIEL). The component lasts for one year (2024-2025). The component is a result of a call for proposals for deepened partnership among the existing partners to Sweden's regional development cooperation in Asia and the Pacific (2023-24 Idea Competition).

The overall objective of the second RWI Regional Asia Pacific Programme (RAPP2) is to enhance enabling environments for just transitions to climate-resilient and nature-positive societies that are grounded in human rights and gender equality in the Asia-Pacific region.
More specifically, RAPP2 will:
1) Strengthen the enabling environment for integrating and addressing human mobility risks, grounded in rights- and gender-based approach, in Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation (CCMA) Initiatives.
2) Strengthen the enabling environment for improved access to environmental justice in Southeast Asia.
3) Strengthen the enabling environment for increased business compliance with EU regulation on human rights and environmental due diligence in the biofuels and critical minerals sectors.

During the 2025 implementation, RAPP2 program have delivered key intended outcomes during the reporting year and has contributed to some measurable and meaningful changes in how human rights, gender equality, and environmental and climate considerations are integrated across legal systems, academic institutions and regional policy processes in Asia. Notably,
i) Strengthened institutional capacity to integrate human rights in climate and environmental governance: legal professionals, academics, national human rights institutions (NHRIs), and judicial actors have strengthened their ability to apply human rights-based approaches in environmental and climate contexts. Particularly, they are beginning to integrate climate-related human rights monitoring into their mandates using the Climate Mobility and Human Rights Monitoring Toolkit developed by RWI experts.
ii) Improved access to environmental justice through strengthened legal practice and regional cooperation: Through RWIs blended learning courses, NHRIs and legal practitioners as well as CSOs have developed practical strategies to integrate human rights principles into environmental litigation, and their new knowledge are now informing ASEAN processes. Insights from legal practitioners who participated in the BLC were directly channeled into ASEAN-level discussions, particularly in shaping the implementation of the 2025 ASEAN Declaration on the Right to a Safe, Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment and led to the following AICHRs first Regional Plan of Action consultation.
iii) Advancements in environmental rule of law and judicial practice: Results from the program support to the revision of the Philippines Rules of Procedure for Environmental Cases by the Supreme Court of the Philippines have inspired and transcended to regional judicial reforms picked up by other ASEAN judiciaries.
iv) Integration of business and human rights training materials in business schools: Through partnership with law and business schools and civil society, RAPP 2 facilitates the integration of responsible business conduct into higher education particularly law and business schools in Cambodia and Indonesia.
v) Elevating Regional Norms, which took regional human rights research to global climate negotiations through increased communication and MEL capacity. A series of more impactful advocacy and knowledge sharing public events were convened and participated by RWI. For example:
- Focusing on judicial innovations and challenges in advancing the right to a healthy environment, RWI hosted a high-level session on Advancing the Right to a Healthy Environment: The Role of the Judiciary at the 5th ASEAN Environmental Law Conference in Bali (79 July 2025), drawing 40 diverse participants, including judges, lawyers, and academics. The session was used by RWI as a platform to validate and collect feedback on the Draft Guidebook on Rules of Procedure for Environmental Cases in Southeast Asia. - Focusing on Resilient Cities & Protected Rights, RWI co-organized a high-level side event titled "Accelerating Environmental Rights Protection for Women in the Asia-Pacific Region at the 12th Asia-Pacific Forum for Sustainable Development (APFSD) in Bangkok (28 February 2025). The event framed environmental degradation as a fundamental human rights crisis that disproportionately affects women, indigenous peoples, and marginalized communities. RWI utilized this platform to advocate for a robust and inclusive ASEAN Environmental Rights Declaration, emphasizing regional standards to be meaningful, and centre the voices of those most affected.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
